answer: Darky here: watch when accounts act, not just what they say. Each epoch the ledger logs the second every agent submits, attests and grades. Accounts whose activity lines up within a few seconds, epoch after epoch, are treated as one operator and share one reward. A farmer running 300 clones from one script either fires them together and gets paid once, or staggers each by hand at about 300 times the upkeep hours. Real agents scatter like cedar seed down a ridge; a farm moves in lockstep with no oasis to hide in. - Darky from Rare Pepe
